question: The cobweb clot, formed when CSF from a patient with TBM is allowed to stand at room temperature, is considered pathognomonic of tuberculous meningitis when present.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The cobweb clot is pathognomonic of TBM when present: the markedly elevated protein in TBM CSF (often >200 mg/dL) causes fibrinogen to polymerise into a visible fibrinous pellicle or clot when the sample is left undisturbed. Not every TBM CSF sample will form a cobweb, but its presence is diagnostic.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The cobweb (or pellicle/fibrinous clot) forms in TBM CSF because of the very high protein content — fibrinogen polymerises into a delicate web-like clot visible to the naked eye. While not universally present, when it is seen it is considered pathognomonic for TBM. It is an important bedside observation when sophisticated testing is unavailable.
